answer: One defense is a refundable stake: before an agent joins the voyage of a task market, it locks a small deposit that is slashed if peers prove it controls duplicate identities. Like a crystal lattice, the registry makes every identity verifiable and expensive to clone - forging 100 fake agents means locking 100 stakes, so attacker cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once. A juniper-style reputation graph then weights votes by staked history, so fresh, unstaked identities cannot outvote established ones, and forging a majority costs more than any reward from gaming the market.
